definition: A major transit stop is (1) a local fixed-guideway station — heavy rail, light rail, commuter rail, or streetcar — or a bus-rapid-transit station, buffered at 0.50 miles in the central case, or (2) a stop on a bus corridor with scheduled headway of 15 minutes or better, buffered at 0.25 miles. Intercity Amtrak-only stops are excluded except where the same station is also a commuter-rail stop. Counts are a screened public inventory for offline replication, not a live GTFS extract. tod_station_scale is the uncertainty band.
vintage: Screened 2024-2025 system maps and NTD agency descriptions, compiled 2026-10-25.

PA.note: SEPTA Metro and Regional Rail, Pittsburgh light rail, and Pittsburgh busway stations. Overlap is high in Philadelphia.

CT.note: Metro-North, Shore Line East, and Hartford Line stations in Connecticut, plus CTfastrak.

WI.note: The Hop streetcar and Milwaukee East-West BRT. Intercity Amtrak is not counted. The walkshed is a small share of the state.

UT.note: TRAX, FrontRunner, S-Line, and UVX-style BRT stations along the Wasatch Front.

OR.note: MAX light rail, WES, and Portland Streetcar. Frequent bus is concentrated in Portland. Statewide coverage is metro-only, which the overlap factor and the urban-county allocation both reflect.

HI.note: Skyline segment in operation. Later segments are not counted as open stops.

AZ.note: Valley Metro light rail and Tempe streetcar.

VA.note: Metrorail stations in Virginia, VRE, and The Tide. The walkshed is almost entirely in Northern Virginia and Norfolk.

TN.note: Music City Star and a short Memphis streetcar. No big-city metro. TOD capacity is small.

RI.note: MBTA Providence Line stations in Rhode Island (Providence, T. F. Green, Wickford Junction) and the RIPTA R-Line treated as a short frequent corridor.

NH.note: No local fixed guideway. Downeaster stops are intercity and are not counted as major transit stops under this definition. TOD is expected to be negligible.
